items.title: 12 killed in separate overnight Madhya Pradesh fires
points: Six members each of two families were killed in separate incidents of fire in Katni and Seoni districts of Madhya Pradesh during Diwali celebrations early on Monday, police said.

In Katni, an earthen lamp triggered a massive blaze inside a three-storey building, killing six people across three generations, including a two-month-old infant who was found dead in his mother’s lap.
According to police, the deceased were identified as Puran Agrawal (77), his wife Chandrakala (74), daughter-in-law Poonam, and granddaughters Arya (14), Anvi (6), and the infant.
Katni superintendent of police (SP) Abhinav Vishwakarma said the fire broke out on the upper floors, situated above a crockery shop.
“Preliminary investigation and survivors informed police that a fire started from an earthen lamp kept near a coffee machine and later spread quickly through the house,” he said.
According to police, the fire broke out in a three-storey building, owned by Kundan Lal Soni (75), at 4.30 am in Chhapara town.

items.title: Little real contact with Modi, but there is some common ground: Sonia Gandhi in memoir Belonging
points: For over a decade, they were top political adversaries, squaring off on India’s electoral battlefield.

Yet, in her 544-page memoir, former Congress chief Sonia Gandhi reveals she has had very little real contact with Prime Minister Narendra Modi, while acknowledging some common ground with the Bharatiya Janata Party leader.
“To this day, I’ve had practically no real contact with him.
We meet at semi-official gatherings-for instance, at the Speaker’s chamber,” she writes in her memoir Belonging, which hits the bookstores on Tuesday.
He tends to look away, avoiding eye contact.” She acknowledges that their ideologies and world view are different.
Sunetra Choudhury is the National Political Editor of the Hindustan Times.

With over two decades of experience in print and television, she has authored Black Warrant (Roli,2019), Behind Bars: Prison Tales of India’s Most Famous (Roli,2017) and Braking News (Hachette, 2010).
Sunetra is the recipient of the Red Ink award in journalism in 2016 and Mary Morgan Hewett award in 2018.

items.title: Pawan Kalyan, Wife Anna Konidala Announce Divorce After 13 Years Of Marriage
points: Andhra Pradesh Deputy Chief Minister and actor Pawan Kalyan and his wife Anna Konidala have announced their decision to part ways after sharing a significant part of their lives together.
According to a statement issued by the Deputy Chief Minister's office, the decision was taken with mutual understanding and respect.
"After sharing a significant part of our lives together, we have decided to part ways with mutual understanding and respect.
Pawan Kalyan, the younger brother of actors Chiranjeevi and Nagendra Babu, made his acting debut with Akkada Ammayi Ikkada Abbayi in 1996.
Pawan married Nandini in 1997, but soon their marriage ended.
He later tied the knot with Renu Desai in 2009, and they parted ways in 2012.
In 2013, Pawan married Anna, who is originally from Russia.
They have two children together, Polena Anjana Pawanova and Mark Shankar Pawanovich.

items.title: Kochi Corporation plans water security assessment to strengthen city’s resilience
points: The multipronged project will address water scarcity and pollution, besides focussing on canal rejuvenation and flood mitigation.
A water security assessment project is being planned for the Kochi Corporation to strengthen the city’s water resilience.

The multipronged project, being developed by Indian Institute of Technology (IIT) Palakkad, will address issues, including water scarcity and pollution, besides focussing on canal rejuvenation, sewage management, and flood mitigation.
The project, which will be implemented with technical support from the Kerala Water Authority (KWA), is expected to be completed in six months.

Once completed, the project is expected to provide a comprehensive framework to guide the planning and implementation of water security projects in the city, said Athira P., associate professor, Department of Civil Engineering, IIT Palakkad.
“Different parts of Kochi face specific issues, be it frequently interrupted water supply, flooding, pollution or an increase in the reporting of water-borne diseases.

items.title: JPMorgan Weighs Big Discount to Lure Lenders for Software Debt
points: (Bloomberg) -- Banks led by JPMorgan Chase & Co. could offer one of the year’s biggest discounts to sell some of the $5 billion in debt for software firm Qualtrics International Inc. that the underwriters were stuck holding a few months ago.
Bankers have scheduled meetings with investors this week to discuss the sale of nearly $2 billion of debt in the high-yield bond market, according to people with knowledge of the matter.

Initial indications are that the debt could be marketed at a coupon of at least 8% and a discounted rate of about 85 cents on the dollar, said the people, requesting anonymity as the talks are private.
Qualtrics, which makes online survey tools, agreed to buy data analytics firm Press Ganey Forsta more than a year ago in a deal valued at $6.75 billion.
Eleven banks committed about $5.3 billion in debt financing for the transaction, and the group started preliminary discussions with investors earlier this year to sell that down.

items.title: Coast Guard Airlifts Four Oil Tanker Crew Members After Suspected Food Poisoning
points: The U.S. Coast Guard evacuated four crew members from a Cyprus-flagged oil tanker off Puerto Rico on Sunday after they reportedly fell ill with suspected food poisoning.

An MH-60T Jayhawk helicopter crew from Coast Guard Air Station Borinquen conducted the rescue approximately one nautical mile south of Vieques, Puerto Rico, hoisting all four mariners from the 328-foot tanker Daibelli.

The operation began after the vessel’s master contacted Coast Guard Rescue Sub-Center San Juan Saturday night to report that four crew members were experiencing symptoms consistent with food poisoning.

“I’m grateful our crew was able to safely evacuate all four mariners and get them to a higher level of medical care.” The crew members were flown to Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport in San Juan, where emergency medical personnel were waiting.
The Coast Guard did not provide further details on the mariners’ conditions or the suspected source of the illness.

items.title: Listening is not enough to protect seafarers’ mental health
points: The Mission to Seafarers’ Seafarers Happiness Index draws directly on accounts of life and work at sea.

The International Transport Workers’ Federation, the International Seafarers’ Welfare and Assistance Network and other organisations also use frontline experience to identify risks and recommend improvements.
This work has made it harder to dismiss loneliness, fatigue, anxiety or burnout as private matters that seafarers must manage alone.
The Maritime Labour Convention, 2006, as amended, affirms every seafarer’s right to a safe and secure workplace, decent working and living conditions, health protection and welfare measures.
It provides a clear basis for treating mental health as part of occupational safety and decent work, not an optional addition to crew welfare.
Dawn Doyley, Registrar of Seafarers, Maritime Authority of Jamaica Connectivity and shore leave are equally important.
Free, dependable communication helps seafarers maintain relationships and seek support before distress reaches a crisis point.
Regular check-ups, confidential access to qualified services onboard and ashore, and practical programmes on stress and coping should be built into employment.

Instead, respondents overwhelmingly identified issues including infrastructure readiness, commercial incentives, fuel availability and the distribution of responsibility across the maritime value chain as the most significant barriers to the progress they…

items.title: Shipbroker’s document delay leads to US$24,000 demurrage settlement, ITIC warns
points: A shipbroker contributed US$24,000 towards a settlement of a demurrage dispute after delays in forwarding key documents complicated a claim between shipowners and charterers, according to a case highlighted by International Transport Intermediaries Club…
The dispute concerned a demurrage claim, valued at approximately US$48,000, which the owners were pursuing against charterers for delays at discharge.
The shipbroker became involved after failing to pass on supporting documents relating to the claim.
However, the broker’s delay in forwarding key documents meant the charterers’ objections did not reach the owners promptly, reducing the opportunity to address any deficiencies in the claim.
As liability and causation were not clear cut, ITIC assisted the shipbroker in negotiating a commercial settlement.
Given the weaknesses in the underlying demurrage claim, the matter was settled with the shipbroker contributing US$24,000, half the value of the claim, towards the owners’ losses.
Mark Brattman, Claims Director at ITIC, commented: “Shipbrokers sit at the centre of the information flow between owners and charterers.

items.title: Weathernews brings offline weather intelligence to the bridge, alleviating navigation connectivity gaps at sea
points: Weathernews Inc. , a global weather intelligence company, has launched Offline mode for SeaNavigator for Master, its AI-powered navigation and optimization support service for ship masters, in response to onboard trial feedback that identified unreliable…

In trial feedback gathered between February and April 2026, masters described weak VSAT coverage in parts of the Southern Hemisphere, latency of more than 1,000 milliseconds, route imports failing on poor connections, and restrictions on satellite services…

If the connection drops during a weather-sensitive passage, the master can lose the live picture at exactly the point it matters most, posing a navigational risk and potentially affecting voyage profitability.

items.title: C-MAP® charts meet NavimetriX: weather, routing and charts, together at last, on every screen on board
points: Soft4Sail and C-MAP®, a leader in digital marine cartography and cloud-based mapping, today announced the integration of C-MAP charts into NavimetriX.
For the first time, sailors can access cartography from C-MAP, live weather and weather routing in a single app, on all five major platforms at once.

Available since October 28, just days before the start of the Route du Rhum on November 1, 2026, the integration enables sailors to plan and navigate both offshore races and cruising adventures using C-MAP charts within NavimetriX.
NavimetriX is the all-in-one navigation app for cruising and racing sailors.
No more switching between a chart app and a weather app: the whole picture is on one screen, on the phone at the helm, the tablet in the cockpit or the computer at the chart table.
“This is the app sailors have been asking us for: their weather, their routing and their vector charts, together, on every device on board.
With C-MAP, NavimetriX delivers exactly that,” said Olivier Bouyssou and Henri Laurent, founders of Soft4Sail.

Let the authorities first frame the constituencies and hold the election in April-May next year,” said Mr. Lakrook.

The Lieutenant Governor administration of Ladakh last month dissolved the Ladakh Autonomous Hill Development Council (LAHDC)-Kargil and announced panchayat and municipal elections on November 21 and the process shall be completed before November 30,…

items.title: KSRTC sees sharp rise in ticket bookings during Deepavali, daily reservations cross 62,000
points: According to KSRTC officials, the corporation recorded an average of around 62,000 seat reservations over the last three days, compared to its earlier daily average of approximately 37,000, during the Deepavali festival last year.

The increase has been attributed to the introduction of additional buses into the online reservation system, expansion of designated pick-up and drop-off points in Bengaluru and an increase in special services to destinations across Karnataka.
The number increased to 65,416 on November 6.
On November 7, bookings stood at 62,499.
The November 6 figure represents an increase of around 77% over the corporation’s earlier daily average of 37,000 reservations, during the festival last year.
Even on November 7, bookings remained significantly higher.
Another factor contributing to the increase in reservations is the introduction of additional designated pick-up points at 15 locations across Bengaluru.

More than 2,000 special buses were scheduled to operate on November 6 and 7 to various destinations across Karnataka to facilitate the movement of passengers during the festive rush, the official added.

items.title: Fisherfolk seek higher compensation for men who died in Murasu cyclone
points: Community leader Nanjil Ravi said that apart from the government compensation, what is needed is proper insurance cover for fishermen.
JOTHI RAMALINGAM Various associations have urged the Chief Minister C.
Joseph Vijay to increase the compensation provided to families of fishermen from Kasimedu who died in the recent Murasu cyclone.
Bharathi said the amount of ₹7 lakh was hardly enough to safeguard the interests of families of those who have lost their sole breadwinners.
The kin of people who died in a hooch tragedy and during a political meeting were provided larger amounts as compensation.
Manivannan of the Chennai Mechanised Boat Owners Assocation, said that the amount was too less.
Usually the ₹7 lakh compensation is split as ₹2 lakh from the welfare fund and ₹5 lakh from the Central government.
The boat owner has also promised to pay ₹2 lakh each to the families,” he said.

items.title: SIR: KRMO flags higher voter deletions in Muslim-dominated constituencies
points: In a statement issued on Monday, the organisation said an analysis of booth-level data released by the ECI, carried out by political research consultancy Sankalp, showed that 27.59% of voters had been deleted across the 10 Assembly constituencies…
This was higher than the State average of 19.45%.
The 10 constituencies had a total of 9,62,359 Muslim voters in the 2025 electoral rolls, of whom 2,46,759, or 25.64%, were deleted during the revision.
Across 64 Muslim-dominated constituencies, more than 8.80 lakh Muslim voters were removed, the organisation said.
Of the 15,15,088 voters deleted as absent across Karnataka, 2,58,770 were Muslims.
Similarly, 1,43,940 of the 7,08,666 voters removed under the “already enrolled elsewhere” category were Muslims, KRMO said, citing Sankalp’s data.
The statement also cited the 10 constituencies represented by Muslim MLAs where deletions were particularly high.
Bengaluru’s Chamarajpet recorded 1,07,722 deletions, followed by Kalaburagi North with 1,05,257, Narasimharaja in Mysuru with 99,367, and Shivajinagar in Bengaluru with 81,230.
